title: Map rubric anchors and verification points before analysis
when_to_use: When the task includes a rubric or defined success metrics for specific comparisons or calculations.
experience:
- Before starting analysis, list all required anchor points, metrics, or comparisons specified in the rubric (e.g., 'campaign 184 Germany share 0.297').
- Design calculation logic and queries to produce those specific outputs.
- Verify each required output against the rubric's expected values (e.g., ROAS=3.66 vs 3.311) and resolve discrepancies.
- If rubric uses a specific time period (e.g., latest month June 2024), filter data accordingly before aggregating.
- Confirm required calculations are not omitted (e.g., coefficient of variation, seasonal index per industry).
checklist: Validate final outputs match rubric values
common_failure_prevented: Missing or mismatched anchor values leads to low accuracy scores (e.g., anchor points not matched in Requirement 3/Criterion 3.1).

title: Ensure campaign-level granularity for multi-dimensional analysis
when_to_use: When analyzing performance across multiple dimensions (e.g., device, geo, keyword) for a set of identified campaigns.
experience:
- Aggregate data at the campaign level first for overall screening and health scoring.
- For each dimension (e.g., device type, geography), compute per-campaign metrics (e.g., cost share, ROAS per device within each campaign).
- Apply segmentation rules (e.g., cost share >35% and ROAS<0.8) within each campaign to flag high-risk sub-dimensions.
- Report findings per campaign, not only across all campaigns (e.g., top 3 geos per campaign, not just overall top geos).
- Ensure results include campaign identifiers alongside dimension-specific metrics.
common_failure_prevented: Aggregating across all campaigns without campaign-specific segmentation leads to missing high-risk patterns per campaign (e.g., no device-level risk identification per campaign in Requirement 3/Criterion 3.2).

title: Compute specified derived metrics before comparative analysis
when_to_use: When the rubric requires specific derived metrics (e.g., coefficient of variation, seasonal index, YoY change) for problem detection or segmentation.
experience:
- Extract all required derived metrics from the task description or rubric (e.g., coefficient of variation, seasonal index per industry).
- Calculate each metric at the required entity level (e.g., per campaign for YoY change, per industry for seasonal index).
- Handle missing data for derived metrics using defined imputation (e.g., backfilling missing YoY values).
- Use derived metrics as inputs for further analysis (e.g., CV to assess volatility, seasonal index to identify patterns).
- Validate that derived metrics are used in subsequent steps (e.g., flag campaigns with rising cost and no ROAS improvement).
common_failure_prevented: Omission of required derived metrics (e.g., CV, seasonal index) leads to incomplete analysis and low scores (e.g., Requirement 4/Criterion 4.2).
